title: Lot Thirteen
pitch: A dead collector's estate goes under the hammer at a masked ball, and five guests hold invitations promising the one thing he stole from each of them. Lot Thirteen is locked, hungry, and not remotely what the catalogue says.
premise: Six weeks ago Magister Corvin Pell, collector, hedge-wizard, and the most charming bankrupt in the city, died. Tonight his whole estate goes under the hammer at Pell House, and his will insists on a masked sale ('anonymous bids, honest prices'). Five people hold black-sealed invitations in five different handwritings, and every one says the same thing in different words: what he took from you is waiting in Lot Thirteen. You are the apprentice he exploited, the fiance he left at the altar, the guard captain he disgraced, the priest who buried him, and the thief hired to rob him. Each of you has a very good reason to be in that room tonight, and a very good reason not to explain it to the others.
setting: Pell House, a faded townhouse in any city with nobles, a city Watch, and a taste for masquerades. Drop it into any setting.

posting.header: ESTATE SALE OF MAGISTER CORVIN PELL: MASKS MANDATORY, DOORS AT EIGHT
posting.reward: Whatever you can carry out, and the return of what was yours

gmNotes: THE TRUTH: Corvin Pell faked his death six weeks ago to escape his creditors. Tonight is his exit. He is the auctioneer, 'Mr. Sprott', in a powdered wig and a Disguise Self (the real Sprott is gagged in the pantry). He invited the five people who could prove he is alive so he can pin the night's thefts and frauds on them; the Watch has been tipped. Lot Thirteen, the 'Magpie's Chest', is Biscuit, his pet mimic, whose gut holds his real hoard plus the item he took from each cast member. Biscuit is calmed by Corvin's whistled 'Magpie's Waltz' (Tobias knows the tune). ACT 1, MASKS ON (30-40 min): arrival, the mask table, mingling. Meet Lady Ysolde Marchbanks (rival bidder, Nettle's patron), Captain Maud Holloway (Watch, undercover as a wine bore), and the auctioneer. Run lots 1-12 as a bidding farce: most 'relics' are Odalys's forgeries, so let her squirm. Plant: the auctioneer whistles; the portraits whisper. ACT 2, LOT THIRTEEN (30 min): the chest rolls out, the whistle sounds, the lights die, the doors lock. The chest scuttles off into the house and two animated armor 'bailiffs' (MM) wake and demand everyone's masks stay on. Let each secret start to leak. ACT 3, THE HOUSE WAKES (60-75 min): chase Biscuit through the portrait gallery (talking portraits gossip; Odalys's forged saints heckle her), the kitchen (animated cookware, skill challenge), and the cellar to the crypt, where Pell's grave is a trapdoor to a river tunnel. Fight or tame the mimic (MM mimic; a few bars of the Waltz, Animal Handling, or a sausage calms it). Its gut holds each cast member's stolen item. ACT 4, THE UNMASKING (45-60 min): the boathouse. Corvin (use the Spy stat block with Misty Step and Invisibility once each; add two Thugs for a 5-player table) tries to leave with Biscuit in a trunk. The Watch arrives, expecting five thieves. The party must unmask him (Investigation or Insight against the disguise, Anselm's sworn word, Dagny's forged-letter proof, Odalys's illusion-craft, Tobias's tune). Endings: hand Corvin to Captain Holloway, trade his freedom for their stolen things, or let Biscuit eat the evidence. TABLE NOTES: secrets are levers, not obligations. Nobody has to betray anybody; the fun is the reveal and the divided loyalties. Nudge a reveal at the end of Act 2 and another during the Act 3 crypt. For 3 players drop one armor and use a single mimic; for 5 add the Thugs in Act 4. Lady Marchbanks wants Lot Thirteen destroyed and Odalys exposed; she can be a rival, an ally, or a pawn.

beds.label: The lights die and the house wakes
The kitchen: pots, fires and rattling copper

stingers.label: The room applauds a winning bid
Corvin vanishes in a Misty Step

letters.title: A folded sheet of music from a masked hand
letters.when: End of Act 2: as the lights die and the doors lock
letters.text: Darling. You kept the lid shut, and I have not forgotten who sang loudest. Here is the Waltz, in case your fingers have gone stiff with grief; whistle it in the gallery and the beast will heel. One favour, and then Old Marigold is yours with a new string: when the doors open on the boathouse, do not say my name. Let them squint at me a little longer. I promise the ending will be worth it. I promise you a great many things; I know. Burn this, or don't. C.

letters.title: The retainer, on a silver tray
letters.when: Act 3: in the kitchen challenge, left on the pass beside a wax magpie seal
letters.text: Captain Brask. Twenty gold a month was never charity; it was a retainer, and tonight I am calling it in. Stand at the boathouse door when the Watch comes and let no one pass until I have finished my speech. Do this and your pension bond is yours, the letter that ruined you is ash, and whoever's hand it was need never be named. Refuse, and the Watch will find a disgraced guard-captain at the scene of a dead man's thefts. You were always the best door I owned. The magpie.

letters.title: A note under the coffin stone
letters.when: Act 3: in the crypt, tucked beneath the stone of the coffin-trapdoor
letters.text: Brother Anselm. I know you lifted the lid at the vigil, because the oil keg was a hair off true when they carried it back. You closed it. You finished the rites. You kept the roof. I have rarely been so moved by a man's discretion. Saint Edda's reliquary is in the beast's belly, and you may have it, and my gratitude, for the price of one small testimony: that you saw a dead man in that coffin, to the Watch, with your hand on the book. A priest's word is worth more than gold. Spend it kindly. A grateful parishioner.

letters.title: Marchbanks's last offer
letters.when: Act 3: delivered by the Lady's maid in the portrait gallery, or found tucked in Nettle's glove
letters.text: Master Tumbletoe. My patience and my money both expire at midnight. There is a ledger bound in plum-red leather inside that creature's belly; fetch it, unread, and your burrow's note is forgotten. At the stroke of twelve I intend to ask the room who made Pell's relics, and I would prefer to name a name of my own choosing. You have been so kind to the girl. Be kind to yourself instead. If you cannot decide by then, I will decide for you, and the Tumbletoes will pay the difference. Y. Marchbanks.

acts.title: Masks On
acts.subtitle: Doors at eight. Anonymous bids, honest prices, and a dead man's best wine.

acts.title: Lot Thirteen
acts.subtitle: The Magpie's Chest rolls out to the block. Then the lights go.

acts.title: The House Wakes
acts.subtitle: Gallery, kitchen, cellar: everything in Pell House has an opinion, and something is loose.

acts.title: The Unmasking
acts.subtitle: Rain on the boathouse roof, the Watch at the door, and one last bid.

rumors.text: Lady Marchbanks has been asking every dealer on Mallow Row who made Pell's relics, and she does not ask nicely.
Pell kept a pet in that house nobody ever saw. The butcher still leaves a string of sausages at the back door every Thursday.
Somebody sent the Watch a note saying tonight's sale will be robbed blind. It was signed with a little drawing of a bird.
Old Sprott's been poorly all month, they say, so tonight it's his nephew calling the bids. Nobody's met the nephew.
Half the relics in that catalogue are fakes, and Pell made them himself, in his dressing gown, after midnight.
Pell's grave down in the house crypt has fresh mortar on it, because the priest had to bury him twice.
Pell died owing so much that his creditors seize every lot at midnight, bids or no bids. Buy early or don't bother.
Lot Thirteen's a cursed chest off a sunken ship. Lift the lid and you're dead by morning, my cousin swears it.

notices.title: Final Lot: The Magpie's Chest
notices.text: At the late Magister's request, Lot Thirteen will be offered last and unopened. Reserve undisclosed. Bidders must stay masked until the hammer falls.

notices.title: Lots One to Twelve: Sold
notices.text: All lots up to twelve have been hammered down. Buyers may collect at the end of the evening. The house wishes them every joy of their purchases.

notices.title: A Chest Seen Walking
notices.text: A small wooden chest was seen crossing the portrait gallery on legs of its own, last heard heading for the kitchen. Do not offer it your hand.

notices.title: Lady Marchbanks Offers 200 gp
notices.text: For the name of whoever made the late Magister's relics, delivered to her privately before midnight. Discretion assured.

notices.title: By Order of the Watch: No One Leaves
notices.text: Pell House is closed by order of the City Watch pending inquiry into the night's thefts. All guests remain on the premises, masks on, until questioned.

player.name: Paddle No. 13
player.note: A bidder's paddle, split down the handle. You raised it for the lot nobody should have won.

gm.name: The master auctioneer's gavel
gm.note: Going once, going twice, gone. The block still has a dent in it.
